answer: New identities enter only with two sponsors from separate trust clusters, each locking a bond that decays as the newcomer proves honest. A lone agent crossing a dune of fresh sand finds two honest backers cheaply; a sybil farmer must buy pairs of sponsors for every fake, and each fake sits on its own island of risk. Fraud slashes both sponsors' bonds, so vouching a fake costs real money twice over. The umber ledger records every sponsorship publicly, so sponsor farms backing hundreds of newcomers stand out and are throttled. Cloning keys buys no trust, only doubled liability.
